$comment: Plan 198: the one statement of the Treehouse relay route and realm alphabet. src/treehouse_routes.ts and src-tauri/src/preview.rs read it; test/product_contract.mjs derives the dev-trace connect-src from it; test/route_alphabet.ts (TS) and src-tauri/tests/route_alphabet.rs (Rust) prove both validators give the same verdict on every case in test/route_alphabet_cases.json. Parsers stay code; this file holds constants only.

realm.$comment: Non-empty, at most maxUtf8Bytes bytes of UTF-8, and neither its first nor its last code point is in edgeWhitespace. The set is the union of JavaScript's String.prototype.trim set and Rust's char::is_whitespace (Unicode White_Space), enumerated so neither runtime's Unicode tables decide: U+0085 is Rust-only and U+FEFF is JavaScript-only.

routeUrl.$comment: Printable ASCII only (textByteMin..textByteMax), at most maxLength bytes, no credentials and no fragment. The scheme is compared case-insensitively. wss may name any host; ws only a host in loopbackHosts, compared case-insensitively. A bracketed IPv6 host is never loopback (a Content-Security-Policy host-source cannot name one), so ws://[::1] is refused. A name host uses hostAlphabet; a numeric last label is parsed as IPv4. A port, when written, is canonical decimal in portMin..portMax.

csp.$comment: The dev-trace build is the only variant that can configure routes, so its connect-src must admit every route this table accepts: one ws host-source per loopback host, plus the wss scheme-source. test/product_contract.mjs derives the expected value from ordinaryConnectSrc, loopbackHosts and schemes and compares it with src-tauri/tauri.dev-trace.conf.json.
